newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen opening higher after data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen opening higher after data.

text.p: U.S. stocks are expected to open higher on Wednesday in reaction to July retail sales and wholesale price data, analysts said.
The Commerce Department earlier said retail sales rose 0.6 percent in July compared with a revised 0.7 percent jump in the previous month. The number excluding automobiles was up 0.5 percent.
Economists in a Reuters survey had expected a 0.7 percent rise in overall retail sales and a 0.5 percent excluding cars.
The producer price index fell 0.1 percent excluding food and energy, the seventh fall in as many months.

Guy Truicko of Unity Management said the figures were better than expect. "Bonds are rallying on the news...I would think (stocks will open) positive, the way stocks have been following bonds. We should look for a higher opening," he said.

Fears that the figures might prompt a U.S. interest rate increase knocked Wall Street overnight, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 101.27 points to 7,960.84, its first close under 8,000 since July 21.
